result.reason: The redline reaches the fallback and most of the preferred position: it creates a mutual aggregate cap using the preferred greater-of formula, retains a mutual consequential-damages exclusion, includes the fallback carve-outs plus fraud and IP infringement, and clarifies that Sparkling’s payment obligations are not damages. It does not expressly carve out data protection or security breaches, unless Sections 13 or 14 cover those obligations, so full preferred compliance is not clear. Drafting is generally professional, though measuring fees from the event giving rise to the claim differs from the preferred claim-date formulation, and the broad statement that Section 15 does not apply to Excluded Claims may also disapply the consequential-damages exclusion rather than merely making those claims uncapped.
